result:
I commented out the ui_off entry, and the close's serial phase now collects: exit 0, where it was exit 4. Commit `6afff5d74` on `w2/W2-13-d10b-tests`.

**sandbox check:** (a) writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-zqvn` was refused (read-only file system) and no file was made. (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` gave `1ae28402a109…` and `git update-index --refresh` worked (exit 0). GOV_TICKET=DAEO-zqvn.
**ps check:** `ps -eo pid,args | grep -iE "[o]llama|[l]lama-server"` shows nothing (exit 1).

- **task:** D-10 gate. Remove the entry of `serial-only.txt` that names no case in a default run (DEC-1112 (3), the CTO's option (a)). W2-13, DAEO-zqvn.
- **status:** DONE
- **work_completed:**
  - **Empty entries found:** I checked all 67 entries with the plugin's own reading (`entries()` and `declares()`). I compared them against a default collection, without `--optin`, of the 37 files the list names (186 cases).
    - **Only one stops the serial phase:** `tests/acceptance/W1-16/test_w1_16_ui_off.py`. It names the whole file, and all 7 of its cases are in `breadth`.
    - **Eight more `file::function` entries name no case in that default collection.** Each is cut to an opt-in list:
      - W1-15 `parallel_scan::…within_the_bound…` (lifted)
      - W1-09 `review::…raced…` (breadth `# cap`)
      - the two W2-69 rebuild cases (lifted: `tests/acceptance/W2-69/`)
      - W1-16 `builtin_allowlist…::…daemon_directory…` (lifted)
      - the two W1-16 `token_rule` cases (lifted)
      - W1-50 `freeze_live_pause::…` (nightly route, lifted-guard)
    - **They don't stop the phase.** The close puts every serial entry on the command line, and `tests/conftest.py:298-306` keeps any case named there by node id. So the plugin's check (`gov_close_serial_only.py:54-60`) finds a case for each of them. It found none for ui_off.
  - **The change:** line 85 is commented out in the file's own style. The comment block states the reason and keeps the old line as `Was: <the line>`.
    - I didn't re-point it: the cap list puts every case of the file in breadth, so there are no default-run node ids to point to.
    - Listing the seven node ids instead would make every default close run them, which undoes D-4's cut.
  - **When the cases do run:** in a run with `--optin=breadth`, ui_off's 7 daemon cases now run in the parallel phase, not serially. The plugin fix (b) restores the serial route, and this line comes back with it.
- **files_changed:** `tests/acceptance/serial-only.txt` (+5, −1).
- **evidence:**
  - **Collection proof:** `serial_check.py` (in my TMPDIR, run through the heavy slot) runs the close's serial-afterwards command from `command.py:922-924` with `--collect-only`. It sets `-p gov_close_serial_only`, `GOV_CLOSE_SERIAL_ONLY_OF` and `GOV_CLOSE_SERIAL_ONLY_GIVEN` to the 48 serial-phase entries.
    - Before: exit 4, `ERROR: no case is named by the entry of tests/acceptance/serial-only.txt: tests/acceptance/W1-16/test_w1_16_ui_off.py` (90/105 collected).
    - After: exit 0, 90/96 collected, 6 deselected.
  - Scratch: 36M, 3096 inodes.
- **tests:** I ran the readers with the change. The 15-minute estimate had already run out, so I compared on HEAD only for `r11_declared_here`, by reading its code rather than re-running it.
  - **Default run** (W2-57 serial_list and nightly_route, `tests/unit/close/test_serial.py`, W1-30's r11/r12/r13 files): 12 passed, 97 deselected by the opt-in cut, 0 failed.
  - **Opted in** (`--optin=lifted,breadth`, same files plus `r11_declared_here`): 131 passed, 1 failed, 27 deselected, 435 s.
    - The failure is `test_w1_30_r11_declared_here.py::test_w1_16_s_daemon_cases_stay_serial_and_its_cases_that_start_no_daemon_are_not_declared`, an opt-in case the brief allows to change. It asserts the W1-16 counts are (94, 67); a collection without `--optin` now gives (6, 36).
    - It isn't caused by my edit: lines 216-225 count from a collect-only without `--optin` and never read the list, so D-4's cut alone makes it red.
    - With the edit, its next assertion (lines 226-227) will also name ui_off's 7 cases as daemon cases not declared serial, once the count is fixed. That is the expected change.
  - The exclusion `-m "not local_only" -k "not real and not green_here and not time_limit"` was on every run; it accounts for some of the deselected cases.
- **discoveries:**
  - **D-4's cut doesn't hold in the serial phase.** The seven serial-route entries above are cut to opt-in lists, but because they are named by node id, a default close still runs them in its serial phase. Several of them run the real gitleaks, which is why they were put in `lifted`.
  - `r11_declared_here`'s W1-16 count is red under D-4's cut whatever the list says.
- **risks:**
  - Until (b), an opted-in run runs ui_off's daemon cases in the parallel phase. They could go red under load there.
  - Any future whole-file entry whose cases are all cut will stop the serial phase again.
- **lessons:** The plugin's empty-entry check fails only for whole-file entries. `file::function` entries are always collected because the conftest keeps cases named on the command line.
- **proposed_decisions:**
  - **The seven cut serial-route entries.** Options:
    - (i) keep them as they are, so a default close runs them;
    - (ii) comment them out like ui_off, so they don't run in a default close but run in the parallel phase when opted in;
    - (iii) let the plugin fix (b) also leave out entries whose cases are all in opt-in lists that aren't opted in.
    - I recommend (iii) inside (b), confidence 0.7.
  - **Who updates `r11_declared_here`'s counts** (94/67) to D-4's cut, and rules on ui_off's route: the CTO.
- **unresolved:** None for the gate.
- **recommended_next_action:**
  - The CTO merges `6afff5d74` into `w2/integrate` and re-runs D-10's serial phase.
  - Then (b), the plugin fix: restore the ui_off line and decide on the seven cut entries.
